title_en: Armenia National Adaptation Funding Facility (Adaptation Fund locally led adaptation grant, AF00000360)

other: Adaptation Fund project ID AF00000360 (single-country locally led adaptation window, formerly Enhanced Direct Access)

implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU) State Agency
national_partners: Ministry of Environment (EPIU is a State Agency under it)
Regional and municipal authorities (through planned Regional Climate Adaptation Committees)
stage: Adaptation Fund proposal approved; implementation start not yet recorded on the Fund's project page
budget_original: USD 4,960,000 requested from the Adaptation Fund = USD 4,660,000 project cost + USD 300,000 implementing-entity fee. Components: 1 = USD 300,000; 2 = USD 500,000; 3 = USD 3,800,000; execution cost USD 60,000 (AF Secretariat technical review, 12 Mar 2025).
cofinancing_note: No co-financing is stated on the Adaptation Fund project page or in the technical-review summary that was read.
summary_en: A four-year Adaptation Fund facility that EPIU would run to pay for small community-led climate adaptation projects in Armenia's regions and municipalities. It also sets up Regional Climate Adaptation Committees, carries out regional climate vulnerability assessments and trains local officials. The Adaptation Fund project page lists the proposal as approved; it records no start date yet.
activities_en: Component 1 (USD 300,000): regional climate vulnerability assessments; translating the National Adaptation Plan and sector plans into region-specific action plans; setting up Regional Climate Adaptation Committees; training 500 regional and municipal officials
Component 2 (USD 500,000): stakeholder mapping and needs assessment, capacity building, knowledge-sharing platforms and networking events

Component 3 (USD 3.8 million): identify, appraise and grant-finance community-led adaptation sub-projects through calls for small project proposals, e.g. drought-tolerant crops and drip irrigation, climate-smart livestock and pasture management, small water harvesting ponds and reservoirs, watershed restoration, reforestation and wetland rehabilitation, climate-resilient buildings and urban drainage, community early-warning systems, solar-powered pumps, small disaster-preparedness infrastructure
Indicative sequence in the proposal: months 1-6 vulnerability assessments, months 7-12 sub-project prioritisation, months 13-36 sub-project execution
results_en: Mid-term milestone (end of year 2): 5 regions, 25 communities, 25 adaptation projects, 250 stakeholders (100 women), 5 knowledge products, 100,000 direct beneficiaries (at least 40% women)
End-of-project target: 10 regions, 50 communities, 50 adaptation projects, 500 stakeholders (200 women), 10 knowledge products, 200,000 direct beneficiaries (at least 40% women)

locations.evidence: Adaptation Fund full proposal (AFB.PPRC.35.33, results framework): target of 10 regions and 50 communities by project end; the regions and communities are not named and are to be selected through the vulnerability assessments and calls for proposals. Stakeholder consultations in the proposal covered Shirak, Kotayk, Gegharkunik, Tavush, Lori, Aragatsotn, Armavir, Ararat, Vayots Dzor and Syunik.

sources.title: Adaptation Fund project page: Armenia National Adaptation Funding Facility
Adaptation Fund Board PPRC.35: Proposal for LLA Single Country Proposal for Armenia (full proposal and technical review, March 2025)
Adaptation Fund country page: Armenia (portfolio of 7 projects)

notes: Stage date: AF project page (read 4 Nov 2026) shows status 'Proposal Approved', approval date 04/11/2025 (format not stated; other dates on the same site are month/day/year, which would be 11 April 2025), duration 4 years, no start date, USD 293,425 transferred. Expected dates 2025-09 to 2029-09 are the proposal's projected calendar (start 1 Sep 2025, mid-term review 1 Sep 2027, closing 1 Sep 2029, terminal evaluation 10 Dec 2029); the real start may have slipped because the portal shows no start date. Marz Adaptation Plans exist only for Tavush and Shirak so far; the other eight are still to be prepared (proposal). The proposal text does not name target communities. This is separate from the two Adaptation Fund land-based adaptation projects (Shirak/Artik and arid zones/forest protected areas), which the Fund lists as under implementation since February 2026. It is also not the GCF early-warning programme SAP068.

title_en: Building Nature-Positive Future for Lake Sevan (GEF-8 / Global Biodiversity Framework Fund, ADB)

other: GEF-8 Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF) project; ADB co-financing TA 10148-ARM and TA 6559-REG

donors: Asian Development Bank (co-financing via technical assistance)
stage: GEF concept (PIF) approved; CEO endorsement and start date not yet recorded
budget_original: GEF project grant USD 1,331,200 plus agency fee USD 119,568. Confirmed co-financing USD 1,400,000 (USD 700,000 ADB TA 10148-ARM + USD 700,000 ADB TA 6559-REG, Cities Development Initiative for Asia). A prospective follow-on ADB investment of about USD 100-120 million is not counted and remains subject to consultations, due diligence and approvals.
cofinancing_note: USD 1.4 million confirmed co-financing from two ADB technical assistance projects; prospective ADB investment of roughly USD 100-120 million not included.
summary_en: A small GEF-8 grant from the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund, to be implemented through ADB with the Ministry of Environment, to support Lake Sevan's environmental sustainability and green infrastructure. It would pay for feasibility, investment planning, engineering design and due diligence for priority sanitation investments that address wastewater-related nutrient and pollution pressure on the lake. It prepares the larger ADB investment programme described in the separate Lake Sevan wastewater record.
activities_en: Feasibility studies and investment planning for priority sanitation investments around Lake Sevan
Engineering design and due diligence for those investments (wastewater-related nutrient and pollution pressures)
Support to Lake Sevan's environmental sustainability and green infrastructure

locations.evidence: GEF project page lists the location only as 'Lake Sevan basin, Armenia'. The marz assignment (Gegharkunik, where the lake and its basin towns lie) is the compiler's inference; the page names no marz, district or community.

sources.title: GEF project 12213: Building Nature-Positive Future for Lake Sevan

notes: Stage date: GEF received the concept 17 Dec 2025 and recorded 'Concept Approved' on 24 Mar 2026. The GEF page does not state components, outcomes, expected CEO endorsement or start date, and the PIF document itself was not opened, so planned components are only described at the level the GEF page gives. This project is also mentioned inside the existing record adb-lake-sevan-resilience-ta-and-gef-nature-positive (a completed-TA record); it is listed here separately because it is a distinct, not-yet-started grant.

title_en: Lake Sevan Basin Wastewater Management investment programme (ADB-supported; proposed ADB loan 60183-001, Lake Sevan Environmental Viability and Advanced Green Engineering Project)

other: ADB 60183-001 (proposed sovereign loan; listing reported by a search index, not confirmed on an opened ADB page)

implementers: Water Committee, Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure
national_partners: Water Committee, Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure
stage: Three-stage programme approved by the Public Investment Committee (1 July 2026); first-phase investment package reported approved; programme in design phase; ADB loan listed as 'Proposed'
budget_original: USD 260 million total cost of the investment programme (news.am, 2 Sep 2026). A proposed ADB loan of USD 100 million from ordinary capital resources is shown in ADB's 'Proposed' project listing according to a search-index summary; that ADB page could not be opened. An earlier feasibility range of USD 80-200 million phased over 20 years was quoted in June 2025 (Hetq).
cofinancing_note: Split between ADB loan, government and other sources is not published in the pages read.
summary_en: A planned multi-stage programme to stop untreated and poorly treated wastewater from reaching Lake Sevan by upgrading the existing treatment plants of Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis with biological treatment, then building plants in medium-sized towns and small plants for rural communities. The Public Investment Committee approved the three-stage programme on 1 July 2026, and ADB is preparing a proposed USD 100 million loan. The total programme cost is reported as USD 260 million and the programme is still in design.
activities_en: Stage 1: upgrade the existing wastewater treatment plants (currently mechanical treatment only) in Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis and add biological treatment
Stage 2: build new treatment plants in medium-sized agglomerations of the Sevan basin
Stage 3: build small stand-alone plants for isolated and small rural communities
Sewerage network expansion: feasibility work (June 2025) foresaw network design of up to 570 km in the basin and decentralised solutions for sewage that is not connected
results_en: Phosphorus discharge into the lake may fall by up to 70 tonnes a year (news.am, 2 Sep 2026, projection)
Feasibility scenario (Hetq, 14 Jun 2025): the more centralised model would route up to 65% of the basin's sewage to the three plants; the less centralised model up to 35%

locations.evidence: news.am (2 Sep 2026): the programme will modernise the treatment plants of Gavar, Martuni and Vardenis; Hetq (14 Jun 2025) names the same three towns as sites of the planned biological plants. Stage 2 and 3 sites (medium towns, small rural communities) are not named in any page read.

The PM press release gives no cost, lender or location for the Sevan programme. The USD 260 million figure and the earlier USD 80-200 million range are not reconciled in the sources.

A consulting agreement for an eight-month feasibility study was signed around May 2025, and an investment package is to go to the Public Investment Committee after the study. Construction dates and financing for the reservoirs themselves are not published.

Environmental and social impact analysis
Basin (watershed) management and modernisation of the downstream irrigation systems
Preparation of an investment package for the Public Investment Committee

title_en: Government of Armenia Programme 2026-2031: water, irrigation, Lake Sevan and forest commitments
national_partners: Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure (Water Committee)
stage: Government programme adopted (announcement-level commitments); no project-level budgets or financing in the source
summary_en: The Government's five-year programme sets national targets for new reservoirs, irrigation, Lake Sevan restoration and afforestation. It is a policy commitment rather than a funded project, and the source gives no budget or lender. It is useful for coordination because it shows where donor programmes are expected to be asked to contribute.
activities_en: Start construction of 10 reservoirs, with completion targeted for 2033
Construct and reconstruct 350 km of canals and pipelines
Introduce an ecosystem-based management model for Lake Sevan and its catchment, including river-ecosystem and biodiversity restoration
Clear forest plantations flooded by Lake Sevan; reduce pollution and improve waste collection on the lake's shore; return illegally occupied areas of Sevan National Park
Carry out afforestation and reforestation; provide 24/7 forest and protected-area protection through the Ecopatrol Service
Cap abstraction from the Ararat Artesian Basin at the legal sustainable yield; promote water efficiency and river-ecosystem protection; introduce a carbon-pricing system (no date)
results_en: 350 km of canals and pipelines built or reconstructed
Irrigation for 10,000 ha of new agricultural land
24-hour water supply in Yerevan, Gyumri and Vanadzor (no date given)
Ararat Artesian Basin abstraction capped at 926 million m3 a year
At least 100 ha of forest plantations flooded by Lake Sevan cleared; Lake Sevan water quality brought to at least 'good' status (no dates)
About 10,000 ha of afforestation and reforestation (no date given)

locations.evidence: ecolur.org summary of the Government Programme 2026-2031: targets are national, except Lake Sevan, Sevan National Park and the cities Yerevan, Gyumri and Vanadzor; reservoir and afforestation sites are not named in the programme text summarised.

sources.title: ecolur.org: Environmental Provisions of the Armenian Government's Programme for 2026-2031

notes: Stage date: programme adopted 2026; the opened ecolur article does not show its own date, and a search-index summary gave 25 August 2026 for adoption by the National Assembly (not verified). Based on a secondary summary on ecolur.org, not the programme text itself. No money, lender or per-site detail is given. The first five of the reservoirs (Artik, Astghadzor, Kasakh, Lichk, Yelpin) are the EBRD Phase 1 package already recorded as ebrd-armenia-water-reservoirs-phase-1; the Prime Minister's press release of 24 Oct 2025 places Kasakh in Armavir marz and Lichk in Syunik marz, which differs from the marz assignment in that record. EVN Report also names Argichi as a sixth reservoir at design stage.

title_en: Armenia Water Compact 2036: national commitments for water security reform (Water Committee)
donors: International financial institutions, donors and private partners (to be mobilised; none named)
implementers: Water Committee, Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure
national_partners: CJSC Jrar Water System Company (irrigation operator)
stage: National commitment document published in 2026; sector strategies and master plan still to be developed and approved; no project financing attached
budget_original: No total amount stated. Indicative split of the 10-year investment programme: about 50% irrigation and drainage modernisation, about 40% water supply, sanitation and wastewater, about 10% flood and drought risk reduction, water-resources management, monitoring and institutional capacity.
cofinancing_note: Financing to come from the state budget, concessional IFI loans, donor grants and, where suitable, private participation and blended finance.
summary_en: A ten-year national water-security commitment issued by the Water Committee, setting outcome targets for irrigation, drinking water and sanitation, groundwater and Lake Sevan protection, and flood and drought risk. It lists priority investments and reforms but no projects, sites or budget. It is the framework that donor water programmes (World Bank WISE, AFD/EU WAIDA, EBRD, ADB) are expected to fit into.
activities_en: Rehabilitate and modernise irrigation infrastructure to cut water losses and energy use; pilot performance-based contracts and blended finance for irrigation
Rehabilitate and extend drinking-water networks, focusing on rural and underserved communities; expand wastewater collection and treatment; prepare a pipeline of bankable wastewater investments
Flood and drought risk reduction and storage reliability, including rehabilitating existing reservoirs and, where justified, building new small and medium-sized reservoirs
Real-time monitoring and a national water informatics system; automated monitoring of Lake Sevan withdrawals; stop over-abstraction in the Ararat Artesian Basin

Reforms: Irrigation Strategy, Water Supply and Sanitation Strategy, National Water Resources Management Strategy, Water Sector Master Plan, Water Code revision, tariff reform, support to Water User Associations and to Jrar, basin management plans for the six Basin Management Areas
results_en: By 2036: water losses in priority irrigation systems down about 50% and energy use for irrigation down about 30%
By 2036: about 200,000 ha of priority irrigation infrastructure modernised; about 250,000-300,000 people with improved irrigation services
By 2036: safely managed drinking water for about 95% of residents (about 2.7 million people); sanitation for about 60% (about 1.4 million people)
By 2036: about 60% of municipal wastewater safely treated; municipal non-revenue water cut to about 45% (from about 55% in 2024)
By 2036: flood and drought risk management improved for about 1.2 million people; digital climate advice and early warning for at least 300,000 water users

locations.evidence: Water Compact 2036 (Water Committee): national targets; named places are only Lake Sevan and the Ararat Artesian Basin / Ararat Valley; priority irrigation systems and basins are not listed.

stage: National targets and action plan approved by ministerial order in 2026; funding and implementing partners not stated
summary_en: National biodiversity plan with five goals and 30 targets under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, approved by the Minister of Environment. Only the forest-related targets could be read: restoring degraded forest ecosystems, raising forest cover and cutting fuelwood demand by 2030. The plan names no budget, donors or regions.

Promote climate-resilient forest management practices; reduce community fuelwood demand
Introduce global indicators and criteria for sustainable forest management (2026-2029)
Promote non-chemical disease control in ArmForest SNCO forest enterprises (2026-2028)
results_en: Target 2: restore at least 15,000 ha of degraded forest ecosystems by 2030
Target 10: increase forest cover by 12,500 ha and cut community fuelwood demand by at least 30% by 2030
